### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/service-storage`, touching **19** documentable anchor(s).

**16** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2a728ba2acf52c13d1918c2afca7b79bf391e1f5`.

⛔ **13** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2a728ba2acf52c13d1918c2afca7b79bf391e1f5` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `cb5acfa9855e8d70c9a862baf6177f4476ea4f66` — the merge of head `4f3c21e550894267d48aff9ac2985567ea2b3c18` into base `2a728ba2acf52c13d1918c2afca7b79bf391e1f5`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin cb5acfa9855e8d70c9a862baf6177f4476ea4f66 && git checkout cb5acfa9855e8d70c9a862baf6177f4476ea4f66
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 2a728ba2acf52c13d1918c2afca7b79bf391e1f5 4f3c21e550894267d48aff9ac2985567ea2b3c18 && git checkout -B drift-repro 2a728ba2acf52c13d1918c2afca7b79bf391e1f5 && git merge --no-ff 4f3c21e550894267d48aff9ac2985567ea2b3c18

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2a728ba2acf52c13d1918c2afca7b79bf391e1f5
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 2a728ba2acf52c13d1918c2afca7b79bf391e1f5` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `4f3c21e550894267d48aff9ac2985567ea2b3c18`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/services/service-storage/src/file-reference-lifecycle.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/file-reference-lifecycle.test.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/file-reference-read-verdict.integration.test.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/storage-service-plugin.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/attachment-access-hooks.ts, content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx + packages/services/service-storage/src/storage-routes.ts (the download door's arms before the verdict and its outage relay), packages/services/service-storage/src/index.ts (the published barrel), packages/objectql/src/engine.ts (`buildSession`, the insert and by-id update hook contexts and their `dispatch.scope`), packages/core/src/security/authz-store-unavailable.ts (the declared envelope and brand), packages/core/src/security/operation-private-keys.ts (`withoutOperationPrivateKeys`), docs/adr/0104-field-runtime-value-shape-contract.md (D3 and the 2026-07-27 ownership addendum), scripts/check-system-context-census.mjs (row 47f's anchor rule), the #25682 lifecycle hunk as it stands on `main` (`systemReadContext`, the quiet answer's precedent), and .changeset/25692-file-reference-claim-read-verdict.md (read for ②). Read-only throughout: the net diff against `main` at the merge base `cb0a2fcf`, the card and its comments, and the head's check-runs.

Face: narrowing (`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on the PR body and the changeset). Review at the PR's requested effort, security card, disclosure discipline in force: mechanism and verdict only.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **`callerContext` exported from `attachment-access-hooks.ts` — right.** The barrel (`index.ts`) does not re-export it and the package publishes `"."` alone, so the export is package-internal and moves nothing on the published surface. The lifecycle reads a write's caller through the same function the attach gates use: the operation context from the write's options with the operation-private keys dropped by `withoutOperationPrivateKeys` from core (the keys belong to the object being written, and the question is about a file's owning record), else the hook session's `userId` / `organizationId` / `positions`. One reading for both modules, as the claim amendment asked.

2. **`judgeFileRead` moved out of `buildFileReadAuthorizer` — right, no behaviour change at the door.** The extracted body is the removed body line for line (53 non-blank lines, equal under whitespace normalisation): the uploader arm, the field-owned arm through `readableFieldOwners` (which honours `fileAccessDelegate` and fails closed), the #25693 organization arm for an unowned file through `isWithinCallerOrganization`, and the attachments arm over the parent records. The door keeps its own request-to-context composition, its `unauthenticated` answer for a caller with no user, and its unchanged `catch` (the authorization-store brand and the API-key lifecycle brand re-raised, every other throw a deny).

3. **The claim path's new deny — right, and it is the door's rule.** `buildFileReferenceReadAuthorizer` mirrors the door's arms before the judgement, in the door's order: a kernel with no `auth` service asks nothing (where the door binds no gate), a `public_read` file is admitted, a caller with no user is refused, then `judgeFileRead` under the write's caller context. `findReferenceableFile` is the one lookup both halves of the path use (copy-on-claim before the write, the claim after it), so the two cannot disagree; it keeps the #25682 organization-scoped lookup first and asks the verdict only when the write has a caller and the plugin bound one. The quiet answer is the #25682 answer exactly: the value is kept as written, nothing is claimed or copied, no new code or status, and the tombstone-revival branch sits behind the same lookup. Each id of a `multiple` field is judged on its own. The declared-constraint check runs after the read check, as the PR body states in one sentence, and the control pins that an admitted caller is still held to the declaration.

4. **The two exemptions — right.** `referencingCallerOf` returns no caller for `!ctx.session` and for `session.isSystem`. In the engine, `buildSession` returns `undefined` when the operation carries no context (a bare kernel, a seed, a provenance-only flow run) and sets `isSystem` only when the context carries it, so the two exemptions are exactly the context-less programmatic write and the system write that census row 47f names, and nothing else. A flow run is either `isSystem` or carries the acting user, so it lands on one of the two declared sides.

5. **The outage envelope — right in the phase that decides the write.** The plugin binding re-raises `AuthzStoreUnavailableError` by brand and answers every other throw as a refusal; the lifecycle does not catch it in copy-on-claim, so the before-hook throw fails the write before the driver runs, and the integration pin reads `code` and `status` off the error rather than writing digits. Precision note, not a defect: the claim in the after phase sits inside the module's existing warn-and-continue net for bookkeeping, so an outage arriving between the two phases of one write is answered there in the closed direction (the file stays unclaimed, a warning is logged) rather than by a thrown envelope. The same file was judged by the same binding in the before phase of that write.

6. **The fail-safe for a write's own copy — right.** The mint record is keyed on `dispatch.scope`, falling back to the hook context itself. In the engine the single-record insert builds one row context and reuses it for `afterInsert` with one `insertScope` shared across both phases, and the by-id update binds `hookContext.dispatch.scope` once for both phases, so the record is found on every engine path. Without it the copy is judged as any unclaimed file and a refusal leaves it unclaimed and retained, the closed direction. The map is weak, so an entry lives as long as its write.

7. **The published surface otherwise — right.** `installFileReferenceHooks` (on the barrel) gains an optional trailing parameter; nothing exported is removed or narrowed. The named type of that parameter, `FileReferenceReadAuthorizer`, is exported from the module but not from the barrel; harmless for a caller, noted for completeness.

8. **System-context census row 47f — right.** Anchored on `file-reference-lifecycle.ts#referencingCallerOf`, the symbol that reads `isSystem`; the row's Get and Lose columns state what the code does. The `Lint · docs & code guards` check-run on this head is green.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@objectstack/service-storage`, with the BREAKING banner, Before / Now / Fix, the ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` in both the PR body and the changeset. This matches what the diff publishes: no spec key, stored row, or exported declaration moves; one optional parameter is added. Per the Post-Task Checklist, a non-protocol breaking change ships `patch` and keeps its banner and disposition. The narrowing holds in both directions: the accept set shrinks only (a record write no longer copies or claims a file its caller may not read), and nothing refused becomes accepted, because the only open arms of the new binding (no `auth` service, `public_read`) are arms the door already leaves open. One consequence inside the declared narrowing: a non-system write whose context carries an organization or a service actor but no user is now refused as the door refuses a caller with no user, and the changeset's Fix line (reference as a caller who may read, or run a deliberate server-side copy as a system write) covers it. The `Check Changeset` check-run on this head is green.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev `open_questions`:** empty; nothing to answer.
- **Dev finding, three acceptance-note candidates handed to the seat thread off GitHub:** not on GitHub and not readable here; they remain the seat's to dispose of and are not covered by this record.
- **Dev finding and PR acceptance note, #25694 to be re-read against this head before dispatch:** concur. That card concerns a different door class, and the binding here now refuses a caller with no user, which bears on that card's first measurement.
- **PR acceptance note, the ADR-0104 D3 text amended in a separate Tier H docs PR:** right that this PR carries no Tier H path. No such docs PR is open at the time of this review. The ADR's D3 Authorization bullet names the download check; the rule this PR implements tightens within the addendum's stated promise (one file, one owning record, one access rule) and reverses nothing, so Prime Directive 13 is met for this landing; the amendment stays owed and stays the maintainer's. Escalated to the seat as an open follow-up.
- **Dogfood:** the one failure named in the PR body is a 5 s timeout under a concurrent gate sweep on an unrelated flow test, green alone; the head's `Dogfood Regression Gate` check-run is green. Accepted.
- **Check-runs on this head at the time of writing:** 32 completed green, 0 red, 5 `Test Core` shards still in progress. The required `Test Core` context is therefore not yet green; this record judges the contract, and the queue reads the checks.
- **One boundary observation on an adjacent, pre-existing path** (not introduced by this diff, not reached through it, closed direction preserved) was escalated to the seat off GitHub under the card's disclosure rule. It does not block.

Ablation legs A to F in the PR body name the pins each leg reddens and the controls that stay green; the counts are consistent with the 15 unit and 11 integration cases read above.
